title: WV 64-17 Food Establishments: 2026 Amendment Summary
body:
## WV 64-17 Food Establishments: 2026 Amendment (what changes for us)

Source: the Notice of Agency Approval filed with the WV Secretary of State on 7/29/2026 (full filing is in Policies & Reference). The Bureau for Public Health says the amendment is "technical cleanup" that brings the state rule in line with the 2022 FDA Food Code. The filing shows no cost to the state or to businesses. It was filed after a public comment period that ended 7/25/2026 with no comments and no hearing. The effective date was not stated in the filing; confirm it with the health department.

### What changes
- **The rule now adopts the 2022 FDA Food Code** (it adopted the 2013 Food Code before). The 2022 Food Code is in Policies & Reference. This is the real change for the kitchen: inspectors will score against the 2022 version.
- **Rule life extended.** The sunset date moves from August 1, 2028 to August 1, 2032. The old 2023 filing and effective dates are struck out.
- **Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).** The exemption list for the manager-certification requirement is reworded. It still exempts packaged-only operations, non-TCS operations, TCS operations that only reheat commercially processed food for immediate service, and temporary establishments. It adds public schools whose district nutritionist holds a CFPM. A full-service kitchen like ours is not exempt, so we still need a certified manager.
- **Food from private homes.** The old cut-leafy-greens refrigeration paragraph (5 C / 41 F within five years) is removed. A new line says food made in a private home, or in a facility exempt from permits and inspection, may not be used to prepare food or be offered to people in a food establishment. Do not accept home-made food for our menu, catering or staff meals.
- **Definition of a food establishment.** Mostly renumbering, plus "TCS food" now replaces "time/temperature control for safety." The private-home exclusion now refers to cottage food as defined in W. Va. Code 19-40-1, instead of the old bake-sale and placard language.
- **Fees section removed.** The separate "Fees" section is gone and the following sections are renumbered. Fees still come from the permit and service fee rules (64 CSR 30 and 64 CSR 51). Confirm whether our fees change.
- **Cleanup.** Minor wording and numbering throughout. "And Human Resources" is struck from the department name.

### Unchanged, and still applies to us
- **Timely correction:** priority items must be corrected at the inspection; if that is not possible, no more than 72 hours. Priority foundation items and HACCP deviations: no more than 10 calendar days.
- **Eggs** that have not been treated for Salmonella must be stored at 41 F (5 C) or colder.
- **Consumer advisory** wording for raw or undercooked meat, poultry, seafood, shellfish and eggs.
- **Construction or remodel plans** must be submitted at least 45 days before work starts.
- **Summary suspension:** the commissioner may suspend a permit for three or more priority items that cannot be corrected on the spot, or for obstructing the inspector.
- **Dogs:** allowed only under the listed conditions (kept out of food areas, signage, insurance, posted cleanup procedure).
- Violation of the rule is a misdemeanor.

### What we should do
- Have the manager skim the 2022 Food Code changes (Annex and Chapters 2, 3, 4) and compare with our SOPs. Update any SOP that cites the 2013 Code.
- Keep the CFPM certificate current and on file (Training & Safety).
- Confirm the effective date and any fee change with the health department.
- Treat anything we cannot check in the filing as unconfirmed.

This is a summary of a filing, not legal advice. The filed rule is the authority.
